title: Code Diff
description: Code Diff helps people inspect source code, structured text, and the destination workflow and review the result before using it in another system.
intro: Code Diff is for a concrete handoff: take source code, structured text, and the destination workflow from a real task, produce the form the next editor, API, document, or workflow expects, and keep enough context to verify what changed.
audience: Developers, QA engineers, code reviewers, and technical writers
input: A representative sample of source code, structured text, and the destination workflow copied from the API, file, codebase, log, document, or request involved in the task.
outcome: A code diff result that preserves the intended meaning and is ready to test in its destination.
review: Check source code, structured text, and the destination workflow, malformed input, escaped values, and destination-specific rules before relying on the result.
bestFor: Small and medium source code, structured text, and the destination workflow samples used for debugging, documentation, migration preparation, review, and reproducible tests.
steps: Paste a representative source code, structured text, and the destination workflow from the task you are working on.
Run Code Diff and compare the first meaningful change with the source.
Inspect source code, structured text, and the destination workflow plus any destination-specific constraints.
Copy or download the result, then validate it in the editor, runtime, API, form, or publishing system where it will be used.
useCases: Code Diff for a real development or integration task rather than a synthetic keyword example.
Preparing Code Diff input and output for a bug report, documentation page, test fixture, or technical handoff.
Using Code Diff to compare the source and result before a migration, import, release, or review.
Code Diff helps catch structural or meaning-changing mistakes before the output reaches another system.

examples.title: Code Diff with a representative sample
examples.description: This Code Diff example uses source code, structured text, and the destination workflow that resembles a small production fixture, so the main change can be checked line by line.
examples.input:
Before: const limit = 10;
After: const limit = 25;

examples.title: Code Diff edge-case review
examples.description: The second Code Diff pass focuses on the part most likely to fail: nested values, escaping, or destination rules.
examples.output:
Line 1 changed: 10 -> 25

Review note: confirm this result in the destination workflow.

tips: Keep the original Code Diff input beside the result until the destination check passes.
Use realistic source code, structured text, and the destination workflow instead of a one-word sample when validating Code Diff.
Do not assume the visual cleanup from Code Diff proves that source code, structured text, and the destination workflow is valid.
Run the normal project, API, schema, browser, or editorial validation after using Code Diff.

faq.question: Who uses Code Diff?
faq.answer: Developers, QA engineers, code reviewers, and technical writers use Code Diff when they need to inspect source code, structured text, and the destination workflow before continuing work in another editor, system, or document.

faq.question: What should I paste into Code Diff?
faq.answer: Paste a focused but representative sample of source code, structured text, and the destination workflow into Code Diff. Include the nesting, punctuation, characters, or edge cases that affect the real task.

faq.question: What does Code Diff change?
faq.answer: Code Diff changes the representation needed for this task. Compare the output with the source to confirm that values and intended meaning remain correct.

faq.question: What should I check after using Code Diff?
faq.answer: After Code Diff, review source code, structured text, and the destination workflow, escaped values, malformed input, and the rules enforced by the destination system.

faq.question: Can I use the Code Diff output in production?
faq.answer: Use the Code Diff result as reviewed working output, then run the destination system's normal validation, tests, schema checks, or editorial review before production use.

faq.question: Does Code Diff store my input?
faq.answer: Code Diff has no account or saved-history feature. Even so, remove passwords, private keys, session cookies, personal data, and production secrets before using any online tool.

keywords: inspect source code, structured text, and the destination workflow
commonMistakes: Running Code Diff with a sample that does not represent the real input.
Using the Code Diff result without comparing it with the original source.
Skipping validation in the editor, runtime, API, or document that receives the output.
